sources.beamwidth: 3GPP TR 36.814/36.942 sector antenna, 65 deg horizontal HPBW
sources.vertical_pattern: 3GPP TR 36.814 vertical pattern form, 10 deg HPBW, 20 dB cap
sources.distance_correction: deneyler/22 method re-derived for the 3GPP antenna (correction.py)
sources.antenna_pattern: 3GPP TR 36.814 Table A.2.1.1-2: A=min(A_H+A_V,25), A_H cap 25, A_V cap 20; chosen after deneyler/22

correction.rule:
- Context: deneyler/22 derived extra_loss(d) = RSRP_model(d) - RSRP_Experia(d) with the cosine antenna. In
  deneyler/23-24 the antenna became the 3GPP pattern but the correction was not re-derived, and RSRP got worse
  (held-out 3.5 -> 5.4 dB). deneyler/25 showed the missing SINR ceiling (transmitter EVM). All of this was
  seen before designing deneyler/26; reported as such.
- Same method as deneyler/22, applied to the 3GPP-antenna model:
  * RSRP_Experia(d): unchanged fit from deneyler/22 (Experia cells of the region, 8 evaluation sites excluded).
  * RSRP_model(d): fit a + b*log10(d) over the measured users of the three deneyler/24 LC_TA runs, using the
    UNCORRECTED RSRP = simulated RSRP + that user's deneyler/22 extra_loss_db. This is exact, because the
    correction is the same on every link of a user (verified in deneyler/22: RSRP change = -extra_loss,
    correlation 1.0) and RSRP does not depend on load or EVM. d = serving distance, clipped 100 m-15 km.
    Only simulation output is used; no Experia value of the evaluation sites.
  * New extra_loss(d) = RSRP_model(d) - RSRP_Experia(d), applied per user as before (measured users: TA
    placement distance; load users: distance to target site).
- Load intervals are copied from deneyler/24 (factor 1.243) and re-calibrated by calibrate.py.

load_calibration.rule:
- Regression: with all new options off the simulator (linked to the private lib with three patches) must
  reproduce deneyler/16 regression_disabled_draw701 byte for byte (after CRLF->LF). Otherwise stop.
- Calibration: the scheduler change lowers the PRB a given traffic needs, so the load factor of deneyler/26
  (1.2432, KPI PRB 0.233) no longer gives the KPI load. Target is the measured load only: mean DL PRB 0.233
  on draw 701 (same inputs and method as deneyler/26: ues_EC_TA_701, load interval = factor / target_prb).
  SINR, RSRP and CQI are NOT used. Round 1 uses 1.2432; while |PRB/0.233 - 1| > 5 % a proportional step
  factor * PRB / 0.233 is taken, at most 4 rounds; the first round within 5 % is frozen, else the last.

rule:
- Model: deneyler/26 FT_TA unchanged (RMa, 3GPP antenna, EVM 8 %, distance correction, 8 dB shadow, TA
  placement) except the buffer-aware PF scheduler (calibrate.py) and the load factor re-frozen by calibrate.py.
- Validation (A): the 3 azimuth draws of deneyler/26 (42/701, 7/702, 99/703), 256 measured users + 72 load
  users. Same decision rule as deneyler/26: held-out RSRP MAE <= 3 dB and SINR MAE <= 3 dB averaged over
  draws, all measured users connected. Reported next to deneyler/26 (old scheduler).
- Voice capacity (B): exactly the deneyler/28 design (AMR 12.2 kbps, 44 B every 20 ms, 3N voice users per
  evaluation site placed from Experia TA, background = the 72 load users at the new frozen factor, SRS
  periodicity 320, steps N = 25, 50, 100, 200, 300 per cell, draw 42/701, 4 s), now with the new scheduler.
  The same voice-user positions as deneyler/28 are used (same random seed), so V25 here vs V25 there shows
  the scheduler effect alone (plus the small background-factor change).
- Criteria as deneyler/28: user can talk if >= 99 % of packets in [1 s, 3.75 s] arrive within 100 ms
  (3GPP TS 23.203 QCI 1, TS 26.132); cell carries its load if >= 98 % of its users can talk (convention of
  3GPP TR 25.814 / ITU-R M.2135, to be checked before citing); no service = not RRC-connected.
